rules.message: Flask request data reaches a shell command. Review the local data flow and avoid shell interpretation.

metadata.remediation: Use a fixed executable with an argument array and shell=False; validate arguments against an allowlist.
metadata.limitations: Intraprocedural Flask args/form/values sources and listed Python shell APIs only; no cross-file flow or custom sanitizer modeling.

rules.message: Flask request data reaches pickle deserialization, which can invoke object constructors and execute code.

metadata.remediation: Use a non-executable format such as JSON with schema validation; never unpickle untrusted request data.
metadata.limitations: Only listed Flask sources and pickle.loads/_pickle.loads are modeled; file-based loads and custom wrappers are not covered.

rules.message: Requests TLS certificate verification is explicitly disabled. Confirm this is not used for production HTTPS traffic.

metadata.remediation: Enable verification and configure a trusted CA bundle instead of verify=False.
metadata.limitations: Direct requests module calls only; Session state and environment configuration are not modeled. HTTP-only or isolated test calls need context review.

rules.message: Flask request data reaches the SQL text of a locally created sqlite3 connection/cursor, rather than a bound value.

metadata.remediation: Keep SQL text constant and pass untrusted values separately using sqlite3 parameter placeholders.
metadata.limitations: Requires the sqlite3 connection/cursor construction in the same scope; not a general database, ORM, or interprocedural SQL rule.

rules.message: Express-style request data reaches Node child_process shell execution.

metadata.remediation: Use execFile/spawn with a fixed executable, an argument array, and shell disabled; allowlist argument values.
metadata.limitations: Inline arrow route callbacks with query/body/params properties only; Express-style route shape is assumed. Named handlers, wrappers, and cross-file flow are not covered.

rules.message: A Node HTTPS/TLS client explicitly disables peer certificate verification.

metadata.remediation: Keep rejectUnauthorized enabled and configure the correct trusted CA certificates.
metadata.limitations: Literal options objects on the listed Node client APIs only; indirect option objects and global environment settings are not covered.

rules.message: Servlet request data reaches JDBC Statement SQL text. Prepared-statement values are not SQL-text sinks.

metadata.remediation: Use PreparedStatement with constant SQL and bound parameters; allowlist any dynamic identifiers.
metadata.limitations: Requires locally available HttpServletRequest and java.sql.Statement types; no ORM, custom wrapper, or cross-method analysis.

rules.message: HTTP request data reaches a Go command configured to interpret shell text. Review whether the command is started.

metadata.remediation: Call a fixed executable directly with separate validated arguments, without sh/bash -c.
metadata.limitations: Named functions with *http.Request parameters and listed sh/bash forms only. Command construction is detected; execution/reachability is not proven.

rules.message: A Go TLS configuration disables the standard certificate-chain and hostname verification.

metadata.remediation: Use normal TLS verification with RootCAs and ServerName; if custom verification is required, review it explicitly.
metadata.limitations: Literal tls.Config initializers only. A correct VerifyConnection callback can intentionally replace standard verification and requires review.

rules.message: A Rust TLS client builder explicitly opts into accepting invalid certificates or hostnames.

metadata.remediation: Remove the dangerous opt-out or pass false; configure trusted roots and the expected hostname.
metadata.limitations: Matches the security-specific reqwest-style method names, not resolved crate identity. Rust grammar support is limited; no macro expansion or Rust taint coverage is claimed.

rules.message: Environment-derived data reaches C/C++ shell execution. Determine who can control this process environment.

metadata.remediation: Do not interpret environment values as shell commands; use a fixed executable and validated argument vector.
metadata.limitations: Unqualified C-library getenv/system/popen forms and local flow only; environment attacker control, pointer aliases, macros, and namespace wrappers are not proven.

rules.message: gets has no buffer-length parameter and cannot limit input to the destination capacity.

metadata.remediation: Replace gets with a bounded input API such as fgets and handle truncation and termination correctly.
metadata.limitations: Legacy unqualified gets calls only; this is not general memory-safety analysis. A project-defined function with this name needs review.

rules.message: Request-controlled data reaches PHP unserialize without a literal prohibition on object classes.

metadata.remediation: Prefer JSON with validation. If legacy serialization is unavoidable, deny object classes and never rely on serialization for trust.
metadata.limitations: Local superglobal/raw-body flow only. The allowed_classes=false control excludes object injection, not every possible resource-exhaustion or application-logic issue.

rules.message: PHP request data reaches a shell-command argument.

metadata.remediation: Avoid shell APIs; use a fixed executable with an argument-vector API and strictly validate each argument.
metadata.limitations: Listed superglobals and shell APIs only; shell-quoting, custom validation, variable functions, and cross-function flow are not modeled.

rules.message: Rails controller parameters reach a single-string Ruby shell-command API.

metadata.remediation: Use a fixed executable with separate validated arguments rather than an interpolated single command string.
metadata.limitations: ApplicationController subclasses and single-argument APIs only; indirect controller inheritance, helpers, and cross-method flow are not covered.

rules.message: Rails controller parameters reach Ruby Marshal object deserialization.

metadata.remediation: Use a non-executable format such as JSON and validate the decoded structure; do not Marshal.load untrusted input.
metadata.limitations: Direct ApplicationController subclasses and listed Marshal methods only; wrappers and interprocedural data flow are not covered.

rules.message: An authorization-style equality guard trusts tx.origin instead of the immediate caller; intermediary contracts preserve tx.origin.

metadata.remediation: Authorize msg.sender through an explicit ownership/role check and review contract-to-contract call behavior.
metadata.limitations: Experimental Solidity grammar: only require/assert equality guards are covered, not modifiers in general, inline assembly, delegatecall, reentrancy, or contract-wide data flow.
